question: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$, verify $A + A'$ is a symmetric matrix and $A - A'$ is a skew-symmetric matrix.
explanation:
First, compute $A' = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$.

$A + A' = \begin{bmatrix} 1+1 & 2+3 \\ 3+2 & 4+4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 5 & 8 \end{bmatrix}$.

Now, $(A + A')' = A + A'$, so it is symmetric.

$A - A' = \begin{bmatrix} 1-1 & 2-3 \\ 3-2 & 4-4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Now, $(A - A')' = A' - A = - (A - A')$, so it is skew-symmetric.

Verified.

options.C: $A+A'=\begin{bmatrix}2&5\\5&8\end{bmatrix}$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric and $A-A'=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$ is symmetric
